title: Create the C++20 build and test scaffold
body:
Establish the smallest buildable repository before server work begins.

Acceptance criteria:
- CMake builds one server executable and one test target
- strict warnings are enabled in development
- Debug sanitizer presets are documented
- CI builds and runs the empty test suite
- README contains exact local build and test commands
baseline: Local assessment on 2026-08-17: CMake builds cache_core and three assertion-based test executables, but a clean build fails while linking cache_server because server.cpp and socket.cpp are absent from its target. The current working tree has no commits or remote, generated build artifacts are untracked, protocol_test.cpp is empty, warnings apply only to cache_core, and CI is not configured. First action: make a clean configure/build/test pass before adding features.

title: Implement a move-only file descriptor wrapper
body:
Build the RAII boundary used by socket ownership.

Acceptance criteria:
- destructor closes an owned descriptor
- copy operations are deleted
- move construction and assignment transfer ownership safely
- get, release, reset, and invalid state are covered by tests
- ownership invariants are documented
baseline: Local assessment on 2026-08-17: Socket already closes in its destructor, deletes copying, and implements move construction and move assignment. It exposes fd(), but release/reset behavior, invalid-state tests, and ownership documentation remain. Preserve this work rather than reimplementing it.

title: Accept and serve one TCP client
body:
Create the smallest observable server path.

Acceptance criteria:
- socket, bind, listen, and accept failures are handled
- one client can connect and receive a PONG response to a temporary minimal request
- client and listening descriptors close cleanly
- manual test instructions are recorded
baseline: Local assessment on 2026-08-17: Server construction already creates, configures, binds, and listens; accept4 requests nonblocking and close-on-exec. The path is not currently linkable or runnable, and handle_message refers to an undeclared _db member. Complete one end-to-end request only after the clean-build gate.

title: Handle multiple clients with poll
body:
Introduce the v1 event loop without advancing to epoll.

Acceptance criteria:
- multiple clients make progress without blocking one another
- readiness and error flags are handled explicitly
- a disconnected peer is removed safely
- connection state has a single clear owner
- an integration test exercises concurrent clients
baseline: Local assessment on 2026-08-17: A poll loop and per-client event mask already exist, and reverse iteration avoids invalidating later indices during erase. EOF from recv currently has only a TODO, non-EAGAIN read/write errors do not close or propagate cleanly, accept errors abort the server, and no concurrent-client integration test exists.

title: Add per-connection input buffering and fragmented-read tests
body:
Make read boundaries independent from request boundaries.

Acceptance criteria:
- each client owns its input buffer
- incomplete data remains available for the next read
- closed peers and read errors do not lose unrelated connections
- tests split representative input at multiple byte boundaries
baseline: Local assessment on 2026-08-17: Client already owns input and output strings and recv appends bytes. Input is never consumed after execution, the current whitespace parser cannot distinguish incomplete input from invalid input, and fragmentation tests do not exist. This should converge with the incremental RESP parser rather than add more ad-hoc parsing.

title: Implement an incremental binary-safe RESP2 parser
body:
Parse the subset needed for command requests.

Acceptance criteria:
- parser reports incomplete, valid, or invalid without conflating states
- arrays and bulk strings are supported
- binary bulk-string content is preserved
- multiple requests can be consumed from one buffer
- invalid lengths and malformed frames return bounded errors
- unit tests exercise arbitrary fragmentation

title: Separate command dispatch from protocol parsing
body:
Keep transport, protocol, and command logic independently testable.

Acceptance criteria:
- parser produces a protocol-level command representation
- dispatcher validates command names and arity
- response formatting is not embedded in storage operations
- PING and ECHO are implemented with unit tests

title: Implement SET, GET, DEL, and EXISTS
body:
Add the first useful in-memory command set.

Acceptance criteria:
- keys and values are binary safe
- missing-key behavior matches documented Redis behavior for the supported subset
- DEL and EXISTS accept the documented arity
- command logic has focused unit tests

title: Implement INCR and DECR with integer edge-case tests
body:
Add integer mutation without undefined behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- missing keys follow the documented initial-value behavior
- invalid integer values return an error without mutation
- overflow boundaries are tested and handled
- successful replies use the correct RESP type

title: Verify basic redis-cli compatibility
body:
Use redis-cli as an external compatibility check.

Acceptance criteria:
- redis-cli connects to the configured host and port
- all currently supported commands work interactively
- one automated or scripted compatibility smoke test is retained
- unsupported behavior is documented rather than implied

title: Support pipelined requests reliably
body:
Allow multiple complete commands to arrive before replies are drained.

Acceptance criteria:
- all complete requests in an input buffer are dispatched in order
- incomplete trailing input is retained
- replies remain ordered
- integration tests combine pipelining with fragmented input

title: Handle partial writes and slow clients
body:
Make output progress independent of send call boundaries.

Acceptance criteria:
- each connection owns queued output
- partial sends retain unsent bytes
- POLLOUT interest is enabled only when useful
- EAGAIN is not treated as a disconnect
- accidental unbounded buffering has a documented limit or policy
- tests exercise a client that drains slowly

title: Implement EXPIRE and TTL
body:
Add documented key expiration semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
- a monotonic clock is used for elapsed-time decisions
- expiration strategy is documented
- expired keys are not returned by supported commands
- overwrite, delete, missing key, and TTL edge cases are tested
- tests avoid timing flakiness where practical

title: Build end-to-end integration test coverage
body:
Test the running server through its TCP boundary.

Acceptance criteria:
- test harness starts and stops the server deterministically
- raw RESP requests and replies are validated
- fragmented requests, pipelining, disconnects, and concurrent clients are covered
- failures leave no orphan server process

title: Run strict warnings, ASan, and UBSan in CI
body:
Make memory and undefined-behavior checks routine.

Acceptance criteria:
- warning-clean build is required
- ASan and UBSan test jobs run in CI
- sanitizer failures fail the workflow
- local reproduction commands are documented
- TSan is deferred unless concurrency is introduced

title: Create a reproducible baseline benchmark
body:
Measure the poll implementation before optimizing it.

Acceptance criteria:
- workload, client count, payload, hardware, and build mode are recorded
- warmup and multiple measured runs are used
- throughput plus median and tail latency are reported when the tool supports them
- limitations and measurement noise are stated
- no superiority claim is made without a valid comparison

title: Document architecture, commands, and known limitations
body:
Make the project understandable and interview-ready.

Acceptance criteria:
- README has build, test, sanitizer, and run instructions
- architecture explains ownership, event loop, parsing, storage, and expiration
- supported-command table states exact behavior
- example redis-cli session is included
- benchmark method and results are linked
- known limitations are explicit

title: Compare epoll only after the poll baseline is stable
body:
This is deliberately post-v1 and must not pull focus from correctness.

Entry criteria:
- fragmented reads, pipelining, partial writes, disconnects, and slow clients are tested
- sanitizer CI is green
- baseline benchmark is reproducible

Acceptance criteria:
- existing connection and parsing interfaces are preserved where practical
- the full test suite passes against epoll
- the same benchmark compares poll and epoll
- results are explained without overclaiming
